> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **213** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9da32a85639c23a3c11a5a297bf82af347b3ea8b` — the merge of head `3284b2fd9c458c79c7e7c6433c34342d51424d3f` into base `cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9da32a85639c23a3c11a5a297bf82af347b3ea8b && git checkout 9da32a85639c23a3c11a5a297bf82af347b3ea8b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c 3284b2fd9c458c79c7e7c6433c34342d51424d3f && git checkout -B drift-repro cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c && git merge --no-ff 3284b2fd9c458c79c7e7c6433c34342d51424d3f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs cd065d3698db13969a28f46bf26f3e47e9ecc09c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3284b2fd9c458c79c7e7c6433c34342d51424d3f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.aggregation-entry.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-mcp-aggregate-filter.dogfood.test.ts + .changeset/28550-mcp-aggregate-entry-filter.md, packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts (`AggregationNodeSchema`, `AggregationFunction`), packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts (`strictUnknownKeyError`), packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts (both `wireBridgeTools` call sites), packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (`callData` aggregate arm), packages/runtime/src/domains/data.ts (the REST query door), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the aggregate verb's `aggregations[i].filter` admission), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Face: narrowing (`record-recognisers --paths` on the four changed paths decides no schema or rules face; the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line decides the narrowing face, so the floor is every non-prose path of the diff). Inputs: the diff `origin/main...origin/claude/project-thread-rgk04t` (two commits over merge base `a2e75562f`), card #28550 and triage 6554150040, QA source #28545, the seat's order, claim 6554573354, dev report 6555058015, the PR body, and the head's check-runs read from the REST API. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no ③ author note is owed.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Which inputs move — the `aggregate_records` aggregation entry, on both transports; nothing else.** Before: `z.array(z.object({ function, field, alias }))`, zod's `.strip` default, inside the top-level `strictToolInput` that closed only the tool's own keys. Now: `z.array(aggregationEntrySchema())`, where the entry is `strictToolInput({ surface: 'this aggregate_records aggregation entry', aliases: { where, filters, conditions → filter; as → alias } }, { function, field, alias, filter })` with the four members taken from `AggregationNodeSchema.shape`. Judged correct: the accept set of the entry becomes exactly the engine node's four declared members, closed.
   - **Widens:** `filter` (the node's `FilterConditionSchema.optional()`) is accepted and forwarded. Correct.
   - **Narrows (a):** every other entry key is refused by name. Named in the record: `where`, `filters`, `conditions` (hinted to `filter`), `as` (hinted to `alias`), the retired `distinct`, and any slip such as `bogusKey`. Before, each was deleted before the handler ran and the call answered. Correct, and it is what the triage asked for.
   - **Narrows (b), not spelled out in the changeset but a consequence of the same line:** a `filter` whose value is not a filter object (a string, an array, a number) is now refused at the door by the node's own shape, where before the whole key was stripped and the unfiltered number served. The unit test pins all three shapes. Correct direction; see ② for the changeset wording.
   - **Unchanged:** `function` is the spec's `AggregationFunction` enum, the same six values the tool enumerated by hand (`count`, `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count_distinct`); the spec enum adds retirement text for two retired spellings only, so the accept set does not move. `field` (`z.string().optional()`) and `alias` (`z.string()`) are byte-equivalent. `.describe` copies the schema and leaves its parse alone.
2. **The refusal names the key and is the top-level refusal's shape.** Both go through the one `strictUnknownKeyError` map (`@objectstack/spec` suggestions.zod.ts): `Unrecognized key(s) on [surface]: [key]. Did you mean [key] → [canonical]?` + the retired-key upgrade-guide sentence + the same `UNKNOWN_ARG_HISTORY` sentence; the SDK adds the path (`at aggregations[0]`) and wraps it as the tool error the file already promises (`isError`, never thrown across the wire). Pinned: `bogusKey` named; entry `where` named with `filter` as the spelling; `distinct` named; bridge never asked in each case. Judged correct.
3. **`filter` reaches the engine as the REST query door hands it — no second evaluator in `packages/mcp`.** The handler forwards `aggregations` whole to `bridge.aggregate`. HTTP bridge (`domains/mcp.ts`) passes `aggregations: o?.aggregations` to `callData('aggregate')`, which hands `aggregations` unchanged to `engine.aggregate` and deliberately resolves the engine itself so the security middleware runs. Stdio bridge (`stdio-data-bridge.ts`) hands `aggregations: opts.aggregations` to `engine.aggregate` after the stored-metadata body/hash refusals, which already collected `aggregations[i].filter` and now actually receive one. Nothing in the diff reads a filter's contents; the grep for a filter evaluator in `packages/mcp` is empty beyond the pre-existing stored-metadata key readers. The REST door (`domains/data.ts`) parses `FindDataRequestSchema`, whose `aggregations` are the same `AggregationNodeSchema`, and forwards the parsed clauses whole. On the engine side one admission serves every filter position (`where`, `aggregations[i].filter`, `having`: `engine.ts` resolves tokens then runs the shared lowering, and the aggregate verb's own `aggregations[i].filter` shape, comparand and declared-type doors), and the security middleware's predicate guard (`predicate-guard.ts` `collectConditionFields` over `aggregations[].filter`, called from `assertReadableQueryFields` on every read AST) is the one that answers `PermissionDeniedError` → 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` for a filter on an unreadable field. The dogfood test pins the admin pair `{ n, all }` equal across MCP and REST and equal to the system-context counts, the grouped case, and the member's 403 on both doors with the MCP error carrying `code: PERMISSION_DENIED`, `status: 403`. Judged correct: the permission answer is the engine's own check, as the ruling required.
4. **Both transports from one file.** `aggregate_records` is registered inside `registerObjectTools`, reached only through `wireBridgeTools` (`mcp-http-tools.ts`), which `mcp-server-runtime.ts` calls once for the long-lived HTTP server (`bridgeDataTools`) and once in the stdio server factory. The stdio bridge attaches `aggregate` only when the engine implements it, and `mcp-stdio-tools.test.ts` already pins `aggregate_records` over stdio. One schema, both doors; the card's claim holds.
5. **Controls.** Entries without `filter` reach the bridge byte-identical (pinned). The top-level alias table is untouched: `metrics`, `aggs`, `aggregates`, `group_by`, `tz`, `timeZone`, and the top-level `filter`/`filters`/`conditions` → `where` still fold into the refusal text (the unit file pins `metrics` → `aggregations`; the existing unknown-argument-keys file pins top-level `filter` → `where`). The same spelling `filter` now means the entry's own member one level down and a near-miss for `where` at the top; the two surfaces are named differently in each refusal, so an agent is told which level it is on. REST is untouched by the diff (no path outside `packages/mcp` and the two tests moves).
6. **First-party callers.** Searched this repo (`skills/**`, `content/docs/**`, `packages/mcp/README.md`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/**`, `.claude/**`, `.github/**`, `packages/qa/**`, `ui/**`) and the sibling checkouts `hotcrm` and `objectui` for `aggregate_records` callers and aggregation-entry literals. Every caller of the MCP tool sends `{ function, field?, alias }` only (`mcp-http-tools.unknown-argument-keys.test.ts`, the scope and stdio tests). The served SKILL text and the skills/docs pages name the tool without listing entry keys; `natural-language-queries.mdx` already says the tool takes a filter. `ui/` never calls the MCP tool: its `{ field, type, label }` entries belong to `ObjectGridAggregationSchema` (a grid-header schema), and its `data-objectstack` aggregate path sends `{ function, field, alias }` over REST. No first-party caller sends `as`, `label`, `name` or any other key the entry now refuses.
7. **`tools/list` declares the narrowing.** The unit file pins the entry's JSON Schema as `additionalProperties: false` with exactly `alias`, `field`, `filter`, `function`, so a client reads the closure and the new member off the schema rather than by being refused. `AggregationNodeSchema` is a `lazySchema` proxy; `.shape` reads through it, and the proxy's JSON-Schema aliasing covers the nested `FilterConditionSchema` (the pin passes per the dev report; the Test Core shards re-read it in CI).

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is the right arm.** `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes (narrowing)` as "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another; both facts are true and both are read". This diff accepts `filter` (widening) and refuses other entry keys and malformed filter values (narrowing). The claim's `yes (widening)` was provisional and the order told the dev to measure; the PR body and the changeset both carry `yes (narrowing)` line-initial, the only spelling the one reader accepts.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.** No `packages/spec` file moves; an MCP tool's argument shape is not something a metadata author writes. Per AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3, `none` takes `patch`, and a breaking non-protocol change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The changeset is `'@objectstack/mcp': patch`, carries `**BREAKING**` in the body, the `fix(mcp)!:` bang in its summary (both carriers `check-adr-0087-registration` reads), both declaration lines, and the PR title carries the same `!`. Judged consistent.
- **ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right in substance and in category.** ADR-0087 governs conversions of stored metadata; an MCP tool call is a request surface, never a stored `sys_metadata` row, so there is no source for a conversion to rewrite — the same disposition the spec records for the retired `distinct` on this very node ("QueryAST is a REQUEST surface"). No export or type moves, so `runtime-interface-only` and `type-surface-only` do not apply. The body's "Before / Now / Who sees it / The remedy" bullets carry no arrow rewrite with code-ish operands under migration framing and no rewrite table, so the detector's four branches do not fire on it (read, not run; the lint family that runs the gate was still in progress at this read).
- **Changeset wording, not a must-fix:** "Who sees it" names only an extra entry key; an MCP client that sent a non-object `filter` value was also answered the unfiltered number and is now refused. The "Before" bullet already says the filter was stripped, so the fact is derivable; the seat may ask for one clause if it wants the changelog line complete, and the review does not turn on it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev `open_questions`: none.** One `out_of_scope_findings` row, answered here: the REST door's entry is still non-strict (`AggregationNodeSchema` is a plain object), so `POST /data/:object/query` keeps stripping an unknown entry key such as `bogusKey` while MCP now refuses it. The order kept REST unchanged and the diff honours that. No wrong answer results on REST (a stripped unknown key changes nothing it computes), so this is not a must-fix of this PR; it is a legitimate follow-up candidate under Prime Directive #12 (one strict contract at the producer) for the seat to card or not — a spec move with its own `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` declaration, not a rider here.
- **`distinct` prescription differs by door.** REST answers the tombstone's sentence (`retiredKey`); MCP answers the generic undeclared-key refusal plus the upgrade-guide pointer, because the entry takes the four live members and not the tombstone, so `tools/list` does not advertise a removed key to agents. MCP never honoured `distinct` (it was stripped), so nothing an MCP client relied on changes meaning. Accepted as designed.
- **CI at this read:** no check red; `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates` and `Test Core (3/8)` completed green, while seven Test Core shards, four Lint families and two Type Check families were still in progress. The landing pre-check (② in the review reference: every check green, not a required subset) is the seat's to re-read before the queue; this record does not stand in for it.
- **Docs drift bot:** the listed pages are flagged on the `count_distinct` literal only; none documents the entry's key set, so none is falsified. The PR body's `Skills-docs: none` line is consistent with the search in ①.6.
- **Dogfood is a private boot** (saves a permission set and loads the MCP plugin); the file says why it does not join the worker-shared showcase. Consistent with the harness's exclusion rule.

### ④ Design judgment

On the narrowing face the question is whether the narrowing takes a declared capability away at the consumer or makes the spec's own refusal real, judged against the published spec on `main`.

- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`: the entry is now literally the spec's `AggregationNodeSchema` members, closed. Nothing a consumer could successfully use is taken away: every refused key was already inert (stripped), and the one key that now works is the one the spec has declared and enforced on the engine since the per-aggregation filter ruling. The change makes the spec's declared member real at the MCP door and makes the strict-input campaign's posture (`#16913`-era `strictToolInput`, refusal-only, named keys, no parsed aliases) reach inside the array. It holds against the code it cites: `strictToolInput` closes with the campaign's message; the handler and both bridges forward `aggregations` whole; the engine's aggregate verb and the security predicate guard do the judging. No `??`, no consumer-side tolerance, no second evaluator — Prime Directive #12 direction.
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.aggregation-entry.test.ts`: judges the tool layer over a recording bridge — forwarding byte-for-byte, refusal before the bridge, the advertised JSON Schema. The two controls (unfiltered entries unchanged, top-level posture unchanged) are the ones the order named. The red-first and two ablations in the dev report (filter member renamed away → 3 red; entry made non-strict → 4 red) match what each case asserts. Holds.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-mcp-aggregate-filter.dogfood.test.ts`: the acceptance scenario from the triage, verbatim — MCP and REST one answer, non-vacuous (`n` below `all`, both equal to the system count), the grouped variant, the unknown key, and the permission-refused field on both doors, with the member's unfiltered count as the control that separates the predicate's refusal from the member's read of the object. The refusal is read off the engine path (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` carried through `errorResultWithCode`), which is what the ruling required. Holds.

No must-fix found.
